question: What would a black hole finishing its evaporation today have weighed when it formed in the early universe?
answer: About as much as a mountain: some 500 billion kilograms, packed into less than the width of a proton. Evaporation time grows with the cube of the mass, so anything much heavier is still here and anything lighter is long gone. Gamma-ray telescopes have watched for their final bursts. None has been seen.
move: Where lifetime climbs steeply with size, the ones ending today share one size.
source: Carr et al., Physical Review D, 2010
reference: Carr, Kohri, Sendouda & Yokoyama, New cosmological constraints on primordial black holes, Physical Review D, 2010
